messages:
anna: Uploaded a compact-row prototype focusing on an inline scope chip and a slide-in invoice drawer for quick downloads. Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/newflow/usage-compact-proto sam: Slide-in drawer is interesting — keeps row tidy but still lets you do bulk actions. Does it work on mobile? Slide-ins can be tricky on small screens. jo: For mobile the drawer becomes a full-screen sheet. On desktop it's a right-side drawer. Keeping CTAs out of the main row reduces clutter. I'll mock both. devon: FYI engineering: slide-in means we can lazy-load invoice payloads only when opened so we avoid extra calls per row. Good for perf. But if customers open multiple drawers concurrently, we need a request queue. anna: Nice. For scope control, instead of global or per-card full pills, propose a tiny inline chip with an icon (org/project) and a tooltip that opens the scope selector. Minimal by default, expand on click. sam: Accessibility: inline chips must have focus outlines and an aria-label like "Scope: Project X, change scope". Also tokens numbers are small — prefer "Approx. tokens" for label and an aria-label with full number. jo: Microcopy suggestion: show invoice affordance as "Invoice 2 Apr 2 $1.1K" in drawer header instead of row. Row just has a chevron that opens drawer. This reduces visual noise. neil: Perf: reuse one floating menu for all rows and insert content into it when opened. Also virtualize row list and recycle DOM nodes. Add a metric to measure extra backend calls when drawer open rate > 10%. devon: Aria pattern we can use:
...
anna: Great. Jo please add the drawer artboard + inline chip variant; Devon add a small perf spike; Sam validate microcopy lengths at 320px; Neil add metrics note. design-bot: schedule review Thursday 4pm. Thanks! :raised_hands:
